name: gstack
summary: gstack turns Claude Code and other coding agents into a 'virtual engineering team' of slash-command roles (CEO review, eng manager, designer, reviewer, QA lead with a real browser, security officer, release engineer), all Markdown skills plus supporting tools.

concerns: Install (README agent-paste prompt): git clone into ~/.claude/skills/gstack and run ./setup (5,258-line bash): installs Bun deps, compiles 5 local binaries, downloads Playwright Chromium, may pull digest-pinned Docker images and (Linux) sudo -n install a font
A bare ./setup registers a default-on global Stop hook in ~/.claude/settings.json (runs bundled code at every session end, every project); plan-tune hooks are a [y/N] prompt defaulting to N
README install prompt asks the agent to add a CLAUDE.md rule 'Never use mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools' (target CLAUDE.md unspecified, may be global)

Team mode commits a CLAUDE.md STOP directive and a Skill|skill PreToolUse blocker to the repo, and auto-updates at most hourly: fetches the mutable stable branch and runs ./setup with no signature check

Update check on by default (git ls-remote, raw VERSION, compare API), asks before upgrading in solo mode; telemetry off by default (opt-in, confirmed in code); outside reviews send code to Codex/Claude by default

Browser skills drive the user's real logged-in browser (Aside); setup-browser-cookies decrypts Chrome-family cookies via the Keychain key; /pair-agent can open an ngrok tunnel to the browser daemon (consent-gated)
/setup-gbrain asks for an account-wide Supabase PAT, can create/delete projects, clones gbrain at unpinned HEAD and registers a user-scope MCP server
Large: 5,012 files

audit.scope: Read-only static review at the pinned revision; nothing executed. Inspected: README install/privacy sections, docs/install.md, docs/uninstall.md, package.json, setup (usage, Bun check, dependency install, font sudo path, CSO image preload, host logic, hook registration 4300-5115 in full), scripts/build.sh, bin/gstack-team-init (full), gstack-session-update, gstack-update-check, gstack-config defaults, gstack-telemetry-sync, gstack-skill-start, gstack-uninstall, gstack-gbrain-install, gstack-codex-probe, lib/claude-code.ts, browse cookie import and server bind, and a sample of the riskiest SKILL.md files (review, ship, land-and-deploy, browse, setup-browser-cookies, pair-agent, setup-gbrain). Not read (about 4,900 of 5,012 files): nearly all of lib/ and ~180 bin/ helpers (incl. the settings-hook writer, ff-update, upgrade, egress and redact libraries), the Chrome extension, CSO native code, Supabase functions, ~55 SKILL.md beyond grep, tests and bun.lock (no dependency audit).
audit.rationale: Its value is in the skill texts, which cannot be used without the global runtime; installing it changes global Claude Code configuration (a default-on Stop hook, optional unverified auto-update in team mode, a CLAUDE.md policy rule), sends code to outside models by default and can drive the real logged-in browser. Any evaluation needs a disposable user or VM, ./setup --no-team --no-timeline-stop-hook --no-plan-tune-hooks --no-browser without the agent-paste prompt, codex_reviews disabled, update_check false, telemetry off, and a before/after diff of ~/.claude/settings.json and CLAUDE.md files. A complete review must still cover the settings-hook writer, update path, egress/redact libraries, extension and bun.lock.

issues.title: Team-mode auto-update fetches and runs unreviewed code at session start
issues.evidence: bin/gstack-session-update:75 THROTTLE_SECONDS=3600; :439 git fetch origin +refs/heads/stable; :577 ( cd "$GSTACK_DIR" && ./setup -q --refresh-registered ); setup:4424-4434 registers the global SessionStart hook; no tag or commit signature check in the update path
issues.exposure: Machines that ran ./setup --team (README calls it recommended): a compromised upstream branch runs code as the user within an hour, silently.
issues.mitigation: Do not use team mode; keep auto_upgrade=false and update manually after reviewing the diff.

issues.title: Setup adds a default-on global Stop hook that runs bundled code in every session
issues.evidence: setup:4874ff registers timeline-stop-hook unless timeline_stop_hook=no; hosts/claude/hooks/timeline-stop-hook runs bun timeline-stop-hook.ts; docs/install.md 'registers one default-on Stop hook'
issues.exposure: Every Claude Code session on the machine after a bare ./setup; it runs whatever later updates place in ~/.claude/skills/gstack.
issues.mitigation: ./setup --no-timeline-stop-hook --no-plan-tune-hooks, only in a disposable HOME; inspect ~/.claude/settings.json afterwards.

issues.title: Install prompt rewrites agent policy through CLAUDE.md
issues.evidence: README.md:38 and :309 'Use /browse from gstack for all web browsing. Never use mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.'
issues.exposure: The paste-to-agent install; the target CLAUDE.md is unspecified and may be the global one.
issues.mitigation: Never use the agent-paste install; do not add the section.

issues.title: Team 'required' mode commits a repository-wide Skill blocker and a STOP directive
issues.evidence: bin/gstack-team-init:79ff 'If GSTACK_MISSING: STOP. Do not proceed.'; :213 matcher 'Skill|skill' with onFailure block; README.md:47 git add .claude/ CLAUDE.md && git commit
issues.exposure: Shared repositories bootstrapped with team mode: collaborators without gstack have every skill blocked; git add .claude/ may commit unrelated files.
issues.mitigation: Do not run gstack-team-init in shared repositories.

issues.title: Outside reviews send repository content to OpenAI or Anthropic by default
issues.evidence: bin/gstack-config:340 codex_reviews defaults to enabled; README.md:286
issues.exposure: /review, /ship, /autoplan and plan reviews when Codex CLI or Claude Code is signed in.
issues.mitigation: gstack-config set codex_reviews disabled; never set GSTACK_CODEX_NO_SANDBOX=1 (bin/gstack-codex-probe:231-236).

issues.title: Browser skills use the real logged-in browser and can decrypt local browser cookies
issues.evidence: browse/SKILL.md:149 'the user's real browser — Aside, with their real cookies and their real logged-in sessions'; browse/src/cookie-import-browser.ts:590 reads the Chrome Safe Storage Keychain key
issues.exposure: /browse, /qa or /design-review with Aside open; /setup-browser-cookies after a Keychain approval. Guardrails are prompt text only.
issues.mitigation: Use only the bundled headless browser (GSTACK_SKIP_ASIDE=1) against local targets; do not run setup-browser-cookies; deny Keychain prompts.

issues.title: /pair-agent can expose the local browser daemon to the internet through ngrok
issues.evidence: pair-agent/SKILL.md:263-275; browse/src/server.ts:148-158 tunnel listener
issues.exposure: Only after /pair-agent remote and a once-per-machine consent with ngrok configured.
issues.mitigation: Do not use.

issues.title: /setup-gbrain takes an account-wide Supabase token, installs unpinned code and registers a user-scope MCP server
issues.evidence: setup-gbrain/sections/brain-init.md:36-45; lib/gbrain-supabase-provision.ts:386 POST projects, :594 DELETE projects; bin/gstack-gbrain-install:42-44 installs default-branch HEAD, :179-183 bun install and bun link; setup-gbrain/SKILL.md:345,387 claude mcp add --scope user
issues.exposure: Only when /setup-gbrain path 2a is chosen; may create paid resources and ingest agent transcripts (consent-gated).
issues.mitigation: Skip; if ever needed use the local PGLite path and revoke any token immediately.

issues.title: Dependency pinning is best effort; some runtime downloads are unpinned
issues.evidence: setup:1915 bun install --frozen-lockfile || bun install --lockfile-only; browse/src/security-classifier.ts:50 huggingface.co/.../resolve/main
issues.exposure: When the frozen install fails, dependencies re-resolve; the classifier model comes from a mutable ref.
issues.mitigation: Evaluate in isolation and verify bun.lock is unchanged after setup.

issues.title: Skills cannot be adopted standalone
issues.evidence: review/SKILL.md has 32 and ship/SKILL.md 46 references to ~/.claude/skills/gstack; every skill starts with bin/gstack-skill-start
issues.exposure: Copying one SKILL.md yields a degraded or failing skill.
issues.mitigation: Use as reference text; agents-digest/gstack-AGENTS.md is the only inert standalone file.

issues.title: Uninstall leaves CLAUDE.md sections, team-mode hooks, gbrain MCP and clone, Supabase project and the Playwright cache
issues.evidence: docs/uninstall.md 'does not edit CLAUDE.md'; bin/gstack-uninstall:17-45 has no MCP or gbrain entries
issues.exposure: After removal.
issues.mitigation: Snapshot ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude.json and CLAUDE.md files before any trial.

issues.title: Linux setup may install packages through passwordless sudo
issues.evidence: setup:1734-1755 sudo -n apt-get install fonts-noto-color-emoji
issues.exposure: Linux hosts with NOPASSWD sudo only.
issues.mitigation: GSTACK_SKIP_FONTS=1.

issues.title: Telemetry is opt-in (ES26 confirmed in code)
issues.evidence: bin/gstack-config:332 telemetry defaults to off; bin/gstack-telemetry-sync:50 exits when off
issues.exposure: Only after a consent answer other than off.
issues.mitigation: Answer off.

audit.reviewer: ES27 security audit (Claude; read-only static review, nothing executed)

name: Claude Code Game Studios
summary: A Claude Code project template that turns a session into a game-development 'studio' of 49 specialized agents (directors, leads, specialists) with 74 slash-command skills, hooks, rules and document templates from brainstorm to launch.

concerns: Project template: adopting means copying the whole .claude/ directory (hooks, permissions, 49 agents, 74 skills, 14 rules) into a project

ES27 correction: .claude/settings.json registers 15 hook commands (15 scripts, 8 events); .claude/hooks holds 18 scripts (the 15, update-check.sh sourced by session-start, the yaml-helper.sh library, and an unwired diagnostic). statusLine also runs a script automatically

update-check.sh: background GET api.github.com/repos/Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios/releases/latest at most once a day; downloads and runs nothing; only a digits-and-dots tag is accepted; writes ~/.cache/claude-code-game-studios/latest-release; off with updates.check: false
67 of 74 skills run a bundled bash/Python bootstrap (yaml-helper.sh) when invoked; skills pre-approve Bash patterns such as Bash(godot *); settings allow python -m pytest *
settings.json denies 130 patterns (rm -rf variants, force push, sudo, .env reads); prefix rules, not a sandbox

audit.scope: Read-only static review at the pinned revision; nothing executed. Read fully: .claude/settings.json, 14 of 15 registered hook scripts, update-check.sh, CLAUDE.md, project.yaml, LICENSE and README setup and safety sections. Control flow and every exit, write, subprocess and network site of validate-commit.sh, validate-push.sh, yaml-helper.sh and statusline.sh. Grep only: the 36 .claude/scripts helpers, all 74 SKILL.md (frontmatter and bootstrap lines extracted for all) and all 49 agents (frontmatter extracted for all). Not read: skill and agent bodies, most of .claude/docs, docs/, studio-tests/, CHANGELOG and UPGRADING.
audit.rationale: No exfiltration, credential access or global configuration change was found in what was inspected, and the only network use is a sanitized, switchable update check. Adoption, however, auto-runs thousands of lines of hook shell and helper scripts and takes over the project's permissions and CLAUDE.md, and the review is incomplete. Use as reference and cherry-pick templates, rules and agent prompts. A whole-kit trial would need a throwaway clone with updates.check false, a full read of validate-commit.sh, yaml-helper.sh and the scripts, and narrower Bash(godot *) and pytest allows.

issues.title: Bundled shell and Python run automatically on almost every tool call and on skill invocation
issues.evidence: .claude/settings.json:150-293 registers 15 hook commands (SessionStart, PreToolUse Bash|PowerShell, Write|Edit, Read, PostToolUse, Notification, PreCompact, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop); 67 SKILL.md files run a !`bash "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../../hooks/yaml-helper.sh" resolve_config` bootstrap
issues.exposure: As soon as Claude Code opens in a project containing this .claude/; upstream changes arrive with every copy or upgrade.
issues.mitigation: Adopt a pinned copy and diff hooks and scripts on upgrade, or remove the hooks block (keep yaml-helper.sh, which the skills call).

issues.title: Daily background update check to GitHub
issues.evidence: .claude/hooks/update-check.sh:45,115-116,132-148 curl/wget api.github.com/.../releases/latest; tag validated to digits and dots; cache in ~/.cache/claude-code-game-studios/latest-release
issues.exposure: Session start when the cache is older than a day, unless updates.check is false or CI is set; reveals IP and usage timing to GitHub.
issues.mitigation: Set updates: {check: false} in project.yaml or project.local.yaml.

issues.title: Two hooks can block tool calls
issues.evidence: .claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh:570-592 (exit 2 on invalid staged data JSON); .claude/hooks/validate-read.sh:109 (exit 2 refuses a whole-file Read of large design documents)
issues.exposure: Commits staging data JSON without Python; reading large design files.
issues.mitigation: Expected behaviour; features.read_guard turns off the read guard.

issues.title: Session-state file is injected into context at every session start
issues.evidence: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh:264-352 previews production/session-state/active.md; session-stop.sh:86 appends it to session-log.md
issues.exposure: Anything written to active.md (by an agent or a cloned project) becomes session context.
issues.mitigation: Treat active.md as instruction-grade content; review it after cloning third-party projects.

issues.title: Skill and settings pre-approvals run project code without a prompt
issues.evidence: .claude/skills/dev-story/SKILL.md:7 Bash(godot *); .claude/settings.json:14 Bash(python -m pytest *)
issues.exposure: godot --script and pytest conftest.py run arbitrary project code while the skill or project is active.
issues.mitigation: Narrow to exact command lines or remove.

issues.title: Web-sourced engine reference can enter always-loaded instructions
issues.evidence: .claude/skills/setup-engine/SKILL.md:3,6,71 WebSearch/WebFetch fill docs/engine-reference; CLAUDE.md:29 @-imports docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md
issues.exposure: Running /setup-engine for an engine version newer than the model's knowledge.
issues.mitigation: Review generated engine-reference files before committing.

issues.title: A hook reads subagent transcripts outside the project (locally)
issues.evidence: .claude/hooks/validate-agent-artifact.sh:61-98
issues.exposure: Every subagent stop; no transmission.
issues.mitigation: None needed.

name: ClaudeAnimationBase
summary: Starter kit for having Claude animate a character with p5.js and p5.brush: an instruction guide the model is pointed at, a renderer (render.mjs), a studio page and a demo scene.

concerns: Needs Node.js, an existing Chrome/Chromium driven through puppeteer-core, and ffmpeg
'Clawd' is an explicit likeness of the Claude Code mascot (ANIMATION_GUIDE.md, docs/views.jpg); the MIT licence cannot grant brand rights (ES27 confirmed)
render.mjs launches Chrome with --allow-file-access-from-files (and --no-sandbox on Linux) and the studio page loads Google Fonts, so agent-written scene code runs with file reads and network access

audit.scope: Read-only static review at the pinned revision; nothing executed and no npm install. Read fully: README, ANIMATION_GUIDE.md (461 lines), render.mjs, gpu_probe.mjs, studio.html, package.json, package-lock.json (every entry: hosts, integrity, install scripts), LICENSE, src/config.js and the core.js setup and render hooks; viewed docs/views.jpg. Drawing code (src/clawd.js, the rest of core.js, sheets.js, demo scene) checked by grep for dangerous browser APIs only; it changes no permissions.
audit.rationale: Small, readable, no hooks, no install scripts and no exfiltration path in the shipped code, so a private local evaluation is low risk. Before using it in a creative pipeline: npm ci from the lockfile, self-host or remove the Google Fonts link and render offline, drop --allow-file-access-from-files if possible, keep --no-sandbox off, and replace the Clawd character (or obtain brand clearance) before publishing anything.

issues.title: The rendering browser runs agent-written JavaScript with local-file reads and network access
issues.evidence: render.mjs:64-67 '--allow-file-access-from-files' (and '--no-sandbox' on Linux); studio.html:6 loads fonts.googleapis.com; src/core.js:307 (0, eval)(v) for --crop-at
issues.exposure: Rendering unreviewed or prompt-injected scene code: page JavaScript could read local file URLs and send them out. On macOS the sandbox stays on.
issues.mitigation: Render only reviewed scene code, self-host the font and render offline, drop the file-access flag.

issues.title: The character is a likeness of the Claude Code mascot; brand rights are not settled
issues.evidence: ANIMATION_GUIDE.md Clawd section 'Clawd is the Claude Code mascot'; package.json:6; docs/views.jpg
issues.exposure: Publishing or monetising output featuring Clawd.
issues.mitigation: Use privately or redesign the character (the guide allows it) before publishing.

issues.title: Dependency ranges are not pinned in package.json
issues.evidence: package.json:11-15 ^2.3.3, ^2.2.3, ^25.11.0; the lockfile pins 46 packages with integrity hashes and no install scripts
issues.exposure: A fresh npm install could re-resolve newer versions.
issues.mitigation: Use npm ci.

issues.title: GPU probe disables the Chrome sandbox on every platform
issues.evidence: gpu_probe.mjs:6 '--no-sandbox'
issues.exposure: Only when run by hand; it loads about:blank.
issues.mitigation: None needed.

name: Spec Kit
summary: Spec Kit is an open-source toolkit that gives AI coding agents structured processes (Spec-Driven Development in core, plus bug-fixing and idea-assessment extensions), reusable templates and composable extensions, presets and workflows.

concerns: CLI installs/updates templates and integrations into projects and coding-agent config; extensions/workflows can run shell tasks and hooks
Community catalogs let users install third-party extensions/presets (supply-chain surface)
MCP surface is experimental and may change

audit.scope: Read-only static review at the pinned revision; nothing executed. About 79k lines of Python; targeted review only. Read: command_init.py (options, extension install, step list, the bundled-workflow and preset sections), _assets.py header, the Claude and Codex integrations in full, events/__init__.py (header, resolve_events, install_integration_events entry), extensions/__init__.py catalog stack and download_extension, shared_infra.verify_archive_sha256, workflows/__init__.py load_custom_steps, the shell step grep, base.py exec-arg helpers, copilot/agy permission flags, github_http.py host allowlist, templates/vscode-settings.json, templates/commands/implement.md hook section, agent-context/extension.yml, both .github/skills SKILL.md files, pyproject.toml and README install. Grep-only for scripts/ and extensions/git/scripts. NOT reviewed: presets, bundles, integrations/installer.py external-package loader, _download_security.py, the 50 other integrations, the full events dispatcher template, the uninstall/upgrade paths, the community catalog entries.
audit.rationale: Suitable after remediation: install a pinned tag, use `specify init --integration claude` (or codex) with no extensions or presets beyond the bundled core, keep the community catalog discovery-only, pass --events false, and review the generated .claude/skills and .specify trees before committing. The review is INCOMPLETE, covering roughly 15% of the Python; the presets, bundles, external integration loader and dispatcher template still need reading before wider use.

issues.title: Extensions can add native auto-running agent hooks
issues.evidence: src/specify_cli/integrations/claude/__init__.py:66 — events_config_file = ".claude/settings.json"; events/__init__.py:1398-1404 writes .specify/events.py (chmod 0o755)
issues.exposure: After `specify extension add` of an extension declaring events:, its scripts run on SessionStart, PreToolUse and similar without an explicit agent action.
issues.mitigation: Install only bundled or reviewed extensions; pass --events false or set integration-events.yml to disable; review .claude/settings.json diffs after any extension install.

issues.title: Third-party extension, preset and step supply chain with optional integrity
issues.evidence: src/specify_cli/shared_infra.py:60 — "Entries without a declared digest are accepted unchanged"; workflows/__init__.py:190 — spec.loader.exec_module(module)
issues.exposure: Installing from a non-default catalog, a URL, or SPECKIT_CATALOG_URL; running workflows with custom steps executes arbitrary Python.
issues.mitigation: Keep the community catalog discovery-only (the default), do not set SPECKIT_CATALOG_URL, avoid custom steps, and pin catalog URLs to a commit if extensions are needed.

issues.title: Mandatory hook instructions make the agent execute extension commands
issues.evidence: templates/commands/implement.md:49 — "After emitting the block above you MUST actually invoke the hook"
issues.exposure: When any installed extension registers optional:false hooks in .specify/extensions.yml.
issues.mitigation: Audit .specify/extensions.yml; use only the bundled core extensions.

issues.title: Unpinned catalogs and no-prompt self-upgrade
issues.evidence: src/specify_cli/extensions/__init__.py:4445 — raw.githubusercontent.com/github/spec-kit/main/extensions/catalog.json; docs/upgrade.md:46 — "Bare specify self upgrade executes immediately"
issues.exposure: Catalog content can change between reviews; upgrade follows releases/latest.
issues.mitigation: Install a pinned tag (uv tool install ... @vX.Y.Z) and avoid self upgrade without review.

issues.title: Copilot integration auto-approves Spec Kit scripts in VS Code
issues.evidence: templates/vscode-settings.json:9-12 — "chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove": {".specify/scripts/bash/": true
issues.exposure: Only when using --integration copilot.
issues.mitigation: Not relevant to Claude Code/Codex; remove the key if Copilot is used.

issues.title: Repository SKILL.md files are maintainer skills
issues.evidence: .github/skills/code-review/SKILL.md:3; .github/skills/add-community-extension/SKILL.md:3
issues.exposure: None
issues.mitigation: Do not register them.

checks.note: GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN attached only to GitHub hosts (github_http.py:22-27); Azure CLI token only for Azure DevOps sources.
Catalog fetches from raw.githubusercontent.com main; GitHub releases latest for self upgrade; extension/preset downloads from catalog URLs. No telemetry found.
The workflow shell step uses shell=True; agent dispatch can add --yolo (Copilot default) or extra args from an env var.
Command templates require the agent to execute mandatory (optional:false) extension hooks (implement.md:39-49).
Extensions declaring events: merge native hooks into .claude/settings.json or .codex/config.toml via the .specify/events.py dispatcher (events/__init__.py:1353-1420); plain init adds none.
init scaffolds from bundled wheel assets with no network (command_init.py:362-366); no post-install scripts found.
Extension and preset archives; sha256 optional (shared_infra.py:54-61); custom workflow steps are Python executed via exec_module (workflows/__init__.py:190).
Writes .specify/ and .claude/skills or .agents/skills in the project; the Copilot integration merges .vscode/settings.json; the hermes integration writes ~/.hermes/skills.
No writes to ~/.claude, ~/.codex, rc files or global git config found for the Claude/Codex paths read; reads ~/.specify config. Not exhaustive.
README installs specify-cli from PyPI (README.md:80); PyPI publisher identity not verified.
Catalog JSON read from the main branch (extensions/__init__.py:4445-4447).
Copilot integration auto-approves .specify/scripts in VS Code (vscode-settings.json:9-12); Claude skills are model-invocable by default.

name: Spec Kit MCP (experimental)
summary: The experimental `specify mcp` command of Spec Kit’s CLI: a local, read-only MCP server that reports the Specify version, project artifacts and installed workflows.

concerns: Experimental surface that may change; installing it means installing the specify-cli Python tool.

audit.scope: Read-only static review at the pinned revision; nothing executed. Read the full MCP server package, the version adapter, the artifact and workflow MCP registration and inventories, and artifacts/mcp_info.py; read docs/overview/mcp.md. artifacts/mcp_list.py, workflows/mcp_list.py, _operation_list.py, _operation_info.py and artifacts/catalog.py were scanned for writes, subprocess, network and dynamic imports rather than read line by line. The underlying ArtifactCatalog -> PresetResolver/ExtensionRegistry read paths were not traced exhaustively.
audit.rationale: The code is clean, read-only and local, but it is only useful if Spec Kit itself is adopted. Keep it as reference-only until the spec-kit toolkit decision is made, then evaluate together with a pinned specify-cli.

issues.title: project_directory not confined to the server launch directory
issues.evidence: src/specify_cli/artifacts/mcp_info.py:271-275 — "launch_directory if tool_input.project_directory is None else Path(tool_input.project_directory)"
issues.exposure: An agent or prompt can enumerate Spec Kit artifact metadata (paths, descriptions) of other projects on disk.
issues.mitigation: Acceptable for local use; launch it from the project root, and treat returned paths as disclosure-level only.

issues.title: Experimental, low-value surface
issues.evidence: docs/overview/mcp.md:3-5 — "experimental. Its command inventory and tool contracts may change"
issues.exposure: Tool contracts may change on upgrade.
issues.mitigation: Pin the specify-cli version if adopted.

checks.note: Tool descriptions are static and benign; results include descriptions from project and extension manifests, which can carry third-party text if community extensions are installed.
No credential reads in the MCP paths; Azure/GitHub auth providers are only used by unregistered operations.
No urllib/http use in the MCP modules; the inventories declare network_access 'none'; catalog-fetching operations are deliberately unregistered (workflows/_mcp.py:12-17).
Only executor.py:73-83 spawns a fixed argv (sys.executable -P -m ... version --json), with no shell.
No writes in the inspected MCP paths; tools carry readOnlyHint annotations.
Requires installing the full specify-cli Python package and the mcp SDK v2 (pyproject.toml:15).
project_directory accepts any absolute path (mcp_info.py:271-275), so it can read Spec Kit metadata outside the launch directory; low impact.

audit.reviewer: ES27 security audit (Claude; read-only static review, nothing executed)

mcp.toolScope: Experimental, read-only: specify_version, specify_artifact_list, specify_artifact_info, specify_workflow_list, plus generic specify_list_commands/specify_describe_command/specify_run_command limited to the 'version' command
mcp.dataAccess: Local project directory (artifact inventory, installed workflow registry); docs state no network access

name: Anti-Slop contrast MCP
summary: A small local MCP server shipped with Anti-Slop’s Claude plugin that checks WCAG contrast between two colours.

concerns: Started automatically by the upstream Claude plugin through a Node launcher that spawns whichever python3/python is on PATH.

audit.scope: Read-only static review at the pinned revision; nothing executed. Read fully: skills/antislop-human/contrast-mcp.py, .claude-plugin/contrast-mcp-launcher.mjs, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, the other plugin manifests (to confirm only Claude declares the server), SECURITY.md, ROADMAP.md (grep). Not tested: Claude Code's actual plugin start-up behaviour.
audit.rationale: Pure local computation with no auth, network or data access. Fine for controlled evaluation if registered manually with a pinned interpreter. Not worth installing the whole plugin for.

issues.title: Starts automatically with the Claude plugin and runs whichever python is first on PATH
issues.evidence: .claude-plugin/plugin.json:13-19 'mcpServers: antislop-contrast: command node ... contrast-mcp-launcher.mjs'; .claude-plugin/contrast-mcp-launcher.mjs:17-19 spawnSync(bin, ['-c','']), :30 spawn(python, [server])
issues.exposure: Every session once the plugin is enabled. A malicious or odd interpreter earlier on PATH would be executed.
issues.mitigation: Don't install the plugin. Register manually with an absolute interpreter and -I, or use contrast-check.py from the skill.

issues.title: Malformed hex accepted, can yield a wrong verdict
issues.evidence: skills/antislop-human/contrast-mcp.py:34-39 (no validation); ROADMAP.md:83 'rejects malformed hex instead of reporting a false pass' (planned v3.2.27)
